summary: Iteration 3 backend retest after fix on RecapRowUpdate.quantite (Optional[Union[str, float, int]]). All 25 tests in test_recap_row_edit.py pass (including the 2 previously failing numeric cases) + 16 regression tests in test_excel_inventory.py. Bonus ad-hoc check: '1 234,5' (FR string with thousand-space + decimal comma) -> 1234.5 OK. Total 41/41 (100%).

minor.issue: Manual recap-row edits persist only in-memory; a backend restart wipes them. Pre-existing, acceptable for MVP.
A manual row with all-empty fields + quantite==0 is silently transitioned to kind='empty' (truthiness-based rule). Pre-existing behaviour, worth documenting.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix confirmed: RecapRowUpdate.quantite typed Optional[Union[str, float, int]] = '' correctly accepts JSON numbers (int/float) AND strings; _parse_quantite handles conversion to float (including FR thousand-space + decimal-comma like '1 234,5' -> 1234.5).
Pre-existing (not in scope): DATASTORE is in-memory only; consider persisting manual recap edits to Mongo for durability.
seed_data_creation: Reused /tmp/sample.xlsx (19780 rows). Tests add/edit/delete recap rows transactionally with cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All recap-row edition and quantite parsing tests are green. Numeric (int/float) and string inputs (incl. FR locale '1 234,5') accepted. No further bugs in this scope.
rca of the issue: Previous 422 was caused by Pydantic v2 strict type validation on quantite: Optional[str] rejecting JSON numbers before reaching _parse_quantite. Fix: changed to Optional[Union[str, float, int]] = '' at server.py:350. _parse_quantite already handled int/float -> float. Confirmed via parametrized tests (42 int, 42.5 float, '42' str, '42.5' str, '42,5' str, '1 000' str) and ad-hoc curl for '1 234,5' -> 1234.5.
